title: Play Detective — Starter Case
subtitle: Fifty questions across five rounds. Swap them for your own.

rounds.title: Opening Statements
rounds.description: Ten to warm the room up. Nobody is out yet.

questions.prompt: Who created Sherlock Holmes?
questions.explanation: A Study in Scarlet, 1887.

questions.prompt: What is Sherlock Holmes’s address?
Sherlock Holmes never says “Elementary, my dear Watson” in any of Conan Doyle’s stories.
questions.explanation: He says “Elementary” and he says “my dear Watson”, but never the two together. The line came later, from the stage and screen.

questions.prompt: Which detective did Agatha Christie make Belgian?
Which of Christie’s detectives is an elderly spinster living in a village?
Which of these is NOT a room on the classic British Cluedo board?
Agatha Christie is the best-selling novelist of all time.
questions.explanation: Somewhere around two billion copies, in more than a hundred languages.

questions.prompt: Who wrote The Big Sleep?
Which private detective did Raymond Chandler create?
questions.explanation: Sam Spade is Hammett’s. It is the single most common mix-up in crime fiction.

questions.prompt: In Murder on the Orient Express, where is the train travelling from and to?

rounds.title: The Evidence
rounds.description: Everything you need is on the screen. Look properly.

questions.prompt: Which of these four fingerprints is a WHORL?
questions.explanation: A whorl has ridges that form complete circles. A is a loop, C is a plain arch, D is a tented arch.

questions.prompt: Which of these four fingerprints is a TENTED ARCH?
questions.explanation: A tented arch comes to a sharp point. B is a plain arch, C is a loop, D is a whorl.

questions.prompt: One of these patterns was made by high-velocity impact spatter — a fine mist of tiny droplets. Which?
questions.explanation: B. A is passive dripping, C is cast-off from a swung object, D is a transfer smear from contact.

questions.prompt: Which pattern is CAST-OFF — blood flung from a moving object?
questions.explanation: C. The drops are elongated and in a line, thrown along the arc of a swing.

questions.prompt: Whose sole made the print found at the scene?
questions.explanation: C. The chevrons match, pointing the same way and the same width apart.

questions.prompt: What does the note say?
questions.explanation: P becomes M, H becomes E, and so on back three: MEET AT MIDNIGHT.

questions.prompt: What word was tapped out in Morse code?
Looking at the floor plan, which exit is nearest the body?
questions.explanation: B, on the library’s west wall, with nothing between it and the body.

questions.prompt: The witness saw a TALL figure, in a HAT, wearing a LONG COAT. Which one is it?
questions.explanation: C is the only one with all three. A has no hat, B’s coat is short, D is not tall.

questions.prompt: Three of these signatures were written by the same hand. Which is the forgery?
questions.explanation: C. A forgery is drawn rather than written, so the line shakes and the pen stops and starts. The others are one confident stroke.

rounds.title: Method
rounds.description: How it is actually done. Typed answers — spelling is forgiven.

questions.prompt: What does DNA stand for?
questions.explanation: Deoxyribonucleic acid.

questions.prompt: In which London district did the 1888 murders attributed to Jack the Ripper take place?
questions.explanation: Whitechapel, in the East End.

questions.prompt: What is the study of insects used to help establish a time of death called?
questions.explanation: Forensic entomology. Which insects arrive, and when, puts a clock on a body.

questions.prompt: Luminol is sprayed at a scene to reveal traces of what?
questions.explanation: Blood. It glows blue where haemoglobin remains, even after cleaning.

questions.prompt: By what name is the headquarters of London’s Metropolitan Police known?
questions.explanation: Scotland Yard — after Great Scotland Yard, its first address.

questions.prompt: Rigor mortis is the stiffening of what, after death?
questions.explanation: The muscles. It sets in over a few hours and passes off over a day or so.

questions.prompt: Which poison was known in Victorian times as “inheritance powder”?
questions.explanation: Arsenic. Cheap, tasteless, and undetectable until the Marsh test.

questions.prompt: What word means evidence that you were somewhere else when the crime was committed?
questions.explanation: An alibi — Latin for “elsewhere”.

questions.prompt: A ballistics examiner matches marks on a fired bullet to what?
questions.explanation: The barrel. Rifling scratches the bullet in a pattern unique to that gun.

questions.prompt: What is the medical examination of a body after death called?
questions.explanation: A post-mortem, or an autopsy.

rounds.title: Motive and Opportunity
rounds.description: Orders, numbers, and one look at a timeline.

questions.prompt: Studying the alibi timeline, who cannot account for 9pm?
questions.explanation: The nephew. Everyone else is covered from 7pm straight through to 11pm.

questions.prompt: Put these four Sherlock Holmes novels in the order they were published, earliest first.
How many Sherlock Holmes SHORT STORIES did Conan Doyle write?
questions.explanation: Fifty-six short stories and four novels — the sixty works of the canon.

questions.prompt: In what year was the first Sherlock Holmes story published?
questions.explanation: A Study in Scarlet, in Beeton’s Christmas Annual, 1887.

questions.prompt: How many rooms are there on the classic British Cluedo board?
questions.explanation: Nine: kitchen, ballroom, conservatory, dining room, billiard room, library, lounge, hall and study.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT one of the six weapons in classic British Cluedo?
In which village does Miss Marple live?
Which Agatha Christie novel caused an outcry over who its narrator turned out to be?
questions.explanation: The Murder of Roger Ackroyd, 1926.

questions.prompt: How many suspects are there in classic British Cluedo?
questions.explanation: Six: Scarlett, Mustard, White, Green, Peacock and Plum.

questions.prompt: Put these detectives in the order their first book appeared, earliest first.
questions.explanation: Holmes 1887, Poirot 1920, Marple 1930, Marlowe 1939.

rounds.title: The Verdict
rounds.description: Harder, worth more, and it ends on a wager.

questions.prompt: On which moor is The Hound of the Baskervilles set?
Which city is Inspector Morse’s beat?
Which city does Ian Rankin’s Inspector Rebus work in?
Who wrote Gone Girl?
Who wrote The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo?
Poirot credits his solutions to his little grey what?
questions.explanation: His little grey cells.

questions.prompt: Columbo’s first name is never revealed in the series.
questions.explanation: Never spoken on screen. It is glimpsed as “Frank” on his police ID in one episode, which fans still argue about.

questions.prompt: In which country is Henning Mankell’s Kurt Wallander a detective?
questions.explanation: Ystad, in the far south of Sweden.

questions.prompt: Which English county was the television series Broadchurch filmed in?
questions.explanation: Mostly around West Bay in Dorset.

questions.prompt: Name the Belgian author who created Inspector Maigret.
questions.explanation: Georges Simenon, who wrote seventy-five Maigret novels.
